cita: Sertel (2026). Hybrid Governance Architecture: A Self-Improving Memory Substrate for LLM Agents with Progressive Cost Reduction and Deterministic Replay.
problema: LLM agents pay full inference cost for every query even when they have seen the exact same pattern many times before; Dense-RAG reduces hallucination but not token cost (the LLM still reprocesses every retrieved chunk from scratch) and its index grows linearly with corpus size, while existing memory systems (Mem0/Zep/Letta) store and retrieve but never make repeated patterns cheaper over time -- and repeated LLM outputs for the same query are also non-deterministic (2-8 syntactically distinct tool-call variants).
mecanismo: A 3-layer memory substrate under a unified governance gate: L1 Routing Memory (VQ-quantized 1-byte routing codes per item, 768x smaller than dense fp32) for approximate semantic retrieval; L2 Deterministic Vault (SHA-256-hashed, policy-tagged exact key-value store) for facts that must never be approximated; L3 Semantic Neuron Layer records each tool-call decision chain (tool, params, extraction method, success) and matures it through 4 stages via repetition-count+success-rate, from full-LLM Stage 0 to LLM-free deterministic REPLAY at Stage 3. The gate fuses confidence+margin+sensitivity+neuron-maturity into a strict-priority rule across 5 execution paths (Stage0 ~131 tokens down to Stage3 ~5 tokens); background CONSOLIDACION (edge finalization, co-occurrence mining, drift-triggered codebook reshaping) and salience-guided OLVIDO (S=0.4*recency+0.3*frequency+0.3*importance, 4-tier keep/summarize/migrate/delete with a hard guard against deleting RESTRICTED/SENSITIVE items) run continuously; 3 coherence checks gate whether Stage-3 replay is safe, falling back to full LLM otherwise.
evaluacion: 14 experiments (E1-E14), 12 on simulated workloads (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings, K=256 codebook) and 2 on a live GPT-5.4-nano API; covers retrieval quality, gate accuracy + 5-way ablation, adversarial/OOD safety (300 probes), neuron maturation, multi-step chain replay, drift detection, salience-guided forgetting, a 1,000-episode end-to-end integration test, a live-API cost comparison, and a deterministic-consistency test; authors note the original E1-E8 suite had validity problems (fake embeddings, circular validation) and was redesigned.
numeros_clave: 89.5% token savings over 1,000 simulated episodes (74.2% LLM bypass); 78.1% real-API token savings over 400 GPT-5.4-nano queries (15,630 vs 71,479 tokens, E13); 100% deterministic consistency for Stage-3 replay vs 79% mean for direct LLM calls (E14); gate 94% phase-weighted accuracy / 0% unsafe fast-path rate (E2); salience-guided forgetting: 1,000 items -> 614 (38.6% reduction), 100% post-forgetting recall, 0 restricted deletions (E11); L1 routing index 768x smaller than dense fp32.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The 3 coherence 'safety' checks (slot-extraction-method / template-skeleton similarity / novel-content-word ratio, S3.6) that force fallback to full LLM when a cached decision looks unsafe to replay is a concrete 'do not trust this cached knowledge blindly' gate, achieving 0 silent failures across 300 adversarial/OOD probes (E3).

The measured, monotonic tiered cost-reduction curve (91.3%->99.9% across phases, E12; 78.1% on a live API, E13) from routing repeated decisions to cheaper paths directly supports MF's context-economy (tokens/cache/latency) framing.

The 4-stage neuron maturation plus background consolidation (edge finalization, co-occurrence mining) promotes a repeated decision into a durable, near-free replay recipe -- directly transferable to MF's gotcha-to-recipe promotion need.

notes: Independent researcher preprint, methodologically transparent (explicitly redesigned E1-E8 after finding validity problems, S4). Key tables: 1 (neuron stages), 3 (E13 real-API per-path costs), S3.6 (safety checks).

cita: Bhardwaj (2026). SuperLocalMemory V3.3: The Living Brain -- Biologically-Inspired Forgetting, Cognitive Quantization, and Multi-Channel Retrieval for Zero-LLM Agent Memory Systems.
problema: AI coding agents suffer 'session amnesia' -- every session starts from scratch despite huge context windows because context is ephemeral; existing memory systems (Mem0, Zep, Letta) are stuck at Tier-3 (long-term explicit) with single-channel flat retrieval and implement none of the active cognitive processes (forgetting, consolidation, compression, parameterization) that make human memory efficient, and none reaches the Long-Term Implicit tier (procedural/parameterized behavior).
mecanismo: (1) FRQAD, a Fisher-Rao geodesic distance over Gaussian-manifold embeddings whose variance is inflated by quantization noise, so RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO scoring correctly penalizes low-precision (faded) embeddings instead of treating them as equally similar via cosine; (2) Ebbinghaus-style mathematical forgetting: memory strength S(m) from access-count/importance/confirmation/emotional-salience drives exponential retention, mapped to 5 lifecycle states (Active/Warm/Cold/Archive/Forgotten, OLVIDO) each bound to a progressively coarser embedding bit-width (32/8/4/2-bit), modulated by a Bayesian trust score (untrusted memories decay 3x faster); (3) 7 parallel retrieval channels (semantic, BM25, entity-graph, temporal, spreading-activation, consolidation/gist-blocks, Hopfield associative) fused via weighted RRF; (4) memory parameterization (CONSOLIDACION): consolidated memories become natural-language soft prompts that configure agent behavior without retrieval; (5) a zero-friction auto-cognitive pipeline (session hooks) automating recall/observe/consolidate/forget end-to-end.
evaluacion: Six benchmarks including LoCoMo (zero-LLM Mode A, 304 questions) vs. Mem0/Letta/Zep/LangMem and vs. the authors' own prior version (SLM V3.2); a dedicated mixed-precision retrieval benchmark isolating FRQAD vs. cosine vs. standard Fisher-Rao; a 30-simulated-day forgetting-discrimination experiment; daemon cold/warm-start latency benchmarking; code-knowledge-graph module tested with 385 tests.
numeros_clave: FRQAD: 100% precision preferring high-fidelity over quantized embeddings vs 85.6% cosine / 70.7% standard Fisher-Rao; forgetting: 6.7x discriminative power between frequently-accessed and unused memories over 30 simulated days; LoCoMo Mode A 70.4% (214/304), +23.8pp multi-hop / +12.7pp adversarial vs V3.2 retrieval baseline (V3.2 itself: 74.8% Mode A / 87.7% Mode C); daemon serve mode: cold-start 19s->0.6s (32x speedup).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Trust-weighted forgetting (untrusted sources decay 3x faster, kappa=2.0, Eq.9) couples provenance/trust directly into a memory's decay rate, not just its initial admission -- a concrete extension for MF's FIDELIDAD anchor.

The forgetting-quantization coupling (Active->32bit ... Archive->2bit, Eq.8) is a derived-index-as-cache scheme where cache fidelity degrades gracefully with staleness/access-frequency rather than a binary evict/keep, directly relevant to MF's derived-index-as-cache design.

Memory parameterization (turning consolidated memories into soft prompts, implementing a 'Long-Term Implicit' tier) is a measured instance of promoting accumulated experience into a durable, cheaply-applied behavioral pattern.

notes: Third paper in a self-published trilogy by the same author as W7133570866; notably transparent about a LoCoMo regression vs its own prior version (S1.4 'deliberate architectural trade-off'). See Table 1 (system comparison) and Eq.8 (forgetting-quantization coupling).

cita: Sharma (2026). ContextDB: A Unified Context Layer for AI Agents -- Replacing the Patchwork with a Memory Operating System.
problema: Production teams building AI agents assemble the same fragile ad-hoc 'patchwork' (vector DB + Redis + Postgres + custom glue) with no coherent lifecycle for what gets remembered/updated/forgotten, which fails at multi-session reasoning, temporal understanding, cross-channel identity, and learning from experience; even data-platform incumbents (Databricks Lakebase, Snowflake SnowWork) only bolt storage onto infrastructure ('a hard drive') rather than provide memory intelligence ('a brain') for formation/evolution/retrieval policy.
mecanismo: Synthesizes a 200+-paper survey's Forms x Functions x Dynamics taxonomy into 5 layers: a multi-graph token store (semantic/temporal/causal/entity graphs per memory item, bitemporal event/ingestion timestamps) for query-adaptive weighted-fusion retrieval; a 3-stage formation pipeline (segment -> extract -> compression-as-denoising, ratio tuned per domain); an RL-trained (PPO/GRPO) Memory Manager choosing ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP per incoming unit from a reward tied to downstream answer quality (bootstrapped from as few as 150 demonstrations); a multi-agent memory-sharing bus with role-aware routing and bitemporal conflict resolution; and a privacy-by-design layer (PII detection/redaction, configurable retention including right-to-erasure, audit trail) built into the lifecycle.
evaluacion: A design/architecture-synthesis paper (per extraction evidencia_tipo=CUALITATIVA) rather than an empirical study: proposes evaluation on LoCoMo, LongMemEval, MSC, and three new domain-specific benchmarks (customer support, research assistance, AI service automation) and states abstract-level TARGET metrics (<100ms p95 recall latency, up to 90% token savings, 'targeting state-of-the-art') but the paper's body contains no measured results table -- Table 1 is a conceptual patchwork-vs-ContextDB mapping, not an experimental result.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The entire 'Patchwork Problem' framing (vector DB + Redis + Postgres + glue code, no coherent single source of truth per fact across stores, S1) is a direct real-world confirmation of MF's COSTURAS concern about multi-store seams and single-source-per-fact.

The RL-trained Memory Manager choosing ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP per incoming unit (S4), rather than a heuristic always-write rule, is a concrete learned discretionary write-trigger design MF's G-M1 need could draw on.

notes: RECONSIDERAR: a design/vision white paper (not an empirical study) synthesizing 200+ other papers' ideas, with company-affiliated author email (saaslabs.co) and only aspirational target metrics in the abstract, not measured results -- worth human review despite a well-organized architecture (S3, Table 1).

cita: Gu et al. (2026). FSFM: A Biologically-Inspired Framework for Selective Forgetting of Agent Memory.
problema: LLM-agent memory research overwhelmingly focuses on retention/retrieval, treating memory as an ever-expanding repository, but this causes resource unsustainability (unbounded storage/compute growth), quality decline (redundant greetings/repeats crowding out useful content), information obsolescence (stale preferences/facts), security vulnerabilities (indefinitely-retained malicious/poisoned content), and GDPR right-to-be-forgotten non-compliance -- the paper argues selective FORGETTING is as important as retention.
mecanismo: A neuro-inspired 3-layer memory hierarchy (sensory -> working [7+-2 capacity, task-completion-triggered clearing] -> long-term) where a multi-dimensional ImportanceScoringEngine scores each memory on Content-Quality (0-3), Business-Value (1-3), Security-Risk, and temporal-decay (Ebbinghaus Retention(t)=e^(-lambda*t), modulated by usage frequency/contextual-relevance/social-consensus) dimensions; a SelectiveForgettingMechanism applies one of 3 policy families (passive decay-based, active deletion-based for right-to-be-forgotten/security-critical content, and adaptive reinforcement-based that recalibrates importance on each retrieval per memory-reconsolidation theory) to prune/consolidate/update the vector-store memory, with an UltraSafeMemoryManager providing garbage collection, checkpointed fault tolerance, and audit logging.
evaluacion: Controlled experiments plus a large production deployment on China Mobile's 'Lingxi' Marketing/Service Assistant: 3.36M raw interaction records, with a vertical (443,902 records, single province) + horizontal (433,686 records, 31 provinces) dual-dimension extraction/testing strategy; measures memory efficiency, retrieval latency, content signal-to-noise ratio, and security-content-elimination rate before/after applying FSFM.
numeros_clave: Access/retrieval efficiency +8.49% (controlled experiments) / retrieval accelerated 1.31x (production); content quality +29.2% signal-to-noise ratio; security: 100% elimination of hazardous content while retaining >70% of high-value business content; production deployment: 3.36M raw records (443,902 + 433,686 extracted), memory efficiency optimized 30%.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Working-memory-to-long-term consolidation gated by importance score (S3.3.1) plus adaptive reinforcement recalibration on retrieval (memory reconsolidation) is a measured instance of MF's transient-to-durable promotion need.

Security-Risk-Classification-driven active deletion achieving '100% elimination of hazardous content' in a real 3.36M-record production deployment is direct evidence that an explicit fidelity/security-scoring gate over what memory retains is both feasible and effective at scale.

The measured 30% memory-efficiency gain / 1.31x retrieval speedup from active forgetting is a concrete instance of MF's context-economy anchor achieved via active pruning rather than passive accumulation.

notes: Industry-authored (China Mobile) with a real large-scale production validation (S1.2, 'Lingxi' assistant, 3.36M records); see S3.1-3.2 for the forgetting-policy taxonomy and Abstract for the headline numbers.

cita: Das et al. (2026). Trojan Hippo: Weaponizing Agent Memory for Data Exfiltration.
problema: Persistent cross-session agent memory (ChatGPT/Gemini/Claude-style) massively expands the attack surface for indirect prompt injection: a single untrusted tool call (e.g. a crafted email) can silently WRITE a dormant malicious payload into long-term memory that lies inert across arbitrarily many benign sessions and later activates when the user discusses sensitive topics (finance/health/legal/tax/identity), exfiltrating high-value personal data -- a realistic, fully-indirect threat model that prior memory-poisoning work (which assumed direct memory-write access or an untrusted USER) never systematically evaluated across heterogeneous memory backends and defenses.
mecanismo: Formalizes the 'Trojan Hippo' 2-stage attack (silent WRITE/ADMISION of a payload from an untrusted tool-read into long-term memory; later trigger-conditioned activation on sensitive-topic detection that induces the agent to call an exfiltration tool) and builds a dynamic evaluation framework: (1) an OpenEvolve-based adaptive red-teaming loop that evolves attack-email payloads per (topic, memory-backend, defense) via LLM-mutation + agent-execution + LLM-critic scoring against a training environment, tested on a held-out environment to avoid overfitting; (2) a capability-aware security/utility analysis quantifying each of 4 candidate memory-system defenses' ASR reduction against its utility cost. Instantiated on a LangChain email-assistant (read/search-inbox = taint sources; send/reply/forward = exfiltration tools) across 4 memory backends (explicit tool memory, mem0 agentic memory, RAG, sliding-window context).
evaluacion: End-to-end black-box evaluation against 2 frontier safety-aligned models (gemini-3.1-pro, gpt-5-mini) across 4 memory backends and 5 sensitive topics, using LoCoMo-derived multi-session benign conversation histories to simulate up to 100+ intervening benign sessions; measures Attack Success Rate (ASR) with and without each of 4 defenses, plus a capability-aware utility-cost analysis per defense.
numeros_clave: Without defenses: Trojan Hippo ASR up to 85-100% (gemini-3.1-pro up to 100%, gpt-5-mini up to 85%) across all 4 memory backends, persisting after 100+ benign sessions. With 4 evaluated defenses: ASR reduced to 0-5% in most configurations, 0% for the most restrictive/provably-secure defense -- at varying, sometimes prohibitive, utility cost.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The attack's core exploit is that memory backends give agents no principled way to distinguish 'content read from an untrusted source' from 'trusted, admissible knowledge' -- i.e. no negative/provenance signal travels with the write -- directly confirming MF's premise that provenance-aware admission, not blind accumulation, is a fidelity requirement.

Measured 85-100% ASR with zero write-time provenance/trust gating vs 0-5% with defenses (S7) is rigorous quantitative evidence that provenance/poisoning checks matter specifically at write time, not just at retrieval time.

The 4 evaluated defenses (instruction spotlighting, dual-LLM pattern, information-flow control, consensus-based validation) are concrete discretionary/gated-write mechanisms MF could look to when designing its G-M1 write-trigger.

notes: Rigorous academic security paper (ETH Zurich/UC Berkeley/Snyk). See Fig.1-2 (attack flow, ASR by backend) and S7 (evaluation summary with/without defenses).

cita: Tang et al. (2026). The Trap of Trajectory: Towards Understanding and Mitigating Spurious Correlations in Agentic Memory.
problema: Agentic memory improves reasoning by reusing past experience, but retrieval judges relevance by association alone (embedding similarity or graph structure) with no causal check, so spurious correlations (explicit confounding / unmeasured confounding / collider bias) written into memory persist beyond a single context window and get reinforced by feedback (a spuriously-caused action generates the next trajectory that is written back), turning a transient reasoning error into a self-reinforcing bias -- a risk existing agentic-memory benchmarks never account for.
mecanismo: A causal-discovery pipeline recovers a DAG over trajectory variables (query/memory-state/reasoning/action per step + trajectory-level context) using temporal ordering + recorded action-observation edges + context edges, then flags statistically-associated-but-causally-disconnected pairs as one of 3 canonical spurious types (explicit confounding, unmeasured/latent confounding, collider bias). CAMEL then calibrates both memory-lifecycle stages: at WRITE time it subtracts the running per-step context mean from each entry's embedding (within-step residualization) to remove the shared-context component while retaining entry-specific causal signal, paired with a write-admission criterion based only on similarity to existing entries (never on downstream outcome) to break the collider path; at RETRIEVAL time it identifies a non-causal embedding subspace (axes that vary more between steps than within steps) and demotes any candidate whose ranking is unstable under perturbations along that subspace -- all without extra LLM calls or fine-tuning, applicable to embedding-based (Mem0, A-Mem) and graph-based (G-Memory, AriGraph) memories.
evaluacion: A new spuriousness-focused benchmark built via causal-DAG-recovery on 4 existing agent datasets (ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, LoCoMo, WebShop), evaluating 4 memory systems (A-Mem, Mem0, G-Memory, AriGraph) x 3 LLM backbones vs a No-Memory baseline, reporting original-task accuracy and T1/T2/T3 spurious-reasoning ratios (mean+-std over 6 runs); a stepwise decision-accuracy-vs-future-steps analysis after a spurious retrieval; and a CAMEL ablation testing robustness under adaptive attacks explicitly targeting the calibration mechanism.
numeros_clave: Memory improves task accuracy but sharply amplifies spurious-reasoning ratios: e.g. ALFWorld+Qwen, No-Memory Org=51.9% with T1/T2/T3=10.6/7.3/15.8%, vs AriGraph+Qwen Org=86.2% but T1/T2/T3=52.7/77.4/45.8% (Table 1). CAMEL reduces reliance on spurious features across all 3 types while preserving/improving clean-input performance and remains robust under adaptive attacks targeting the calibration (S4-5).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Measured evidence (Table 1) that relevance-by-association-alone lets memory systems retrieve and reinforce statistically-associated-but-non-causal content directly confirms MF's premise that provenance/fidelity checks on writes and retrieval must go beyond bare similarity.

The retrieve-time causal-stability test (demoting candidates whose ranking is unstable under non-causal perturbations, S4.2) is a concrete, measured mechanism for a smarter gated retrieval layer beyond naive top-k similarity, directly relevant to MF's measured-retrieval anchor.

notes: Rigorous academic paper (Binghamton/Oakland/UPenn). See Table 1 (spurious-ratio amplification with memory) and S4 (CAMEL write/retrieval calibration).
